messages:
Maria: Heads-up: after the kernel selector change this morning, reranker/emb endpoints show higher p95 on small-item batches. noticed jump on p95 ~15-20%. can we triage batching + token budget?

Alex: got the alert. grabbed a couple profiler dumps. immediate suspect is fewer coalesced tiny requests — continuous window still at 70ms which is too agressive for current arrival pattern. perf snapshot below.

perf-bot: profile summary for endpoint=/v1/embeddings/rerank model=redwood/rerank-lite-3b
``
window_mode: continuous (70ms)
small_batch_ratio: 61%
avg_batch_size: 1.8
p50: 20ms -> 22ms
p95: 50ms -> 59ms
kernel_before: tensor_core_mha_v2
kernel_after: generic_attention_v1
GPU_util: 69% -> 63%
heat: attention kernel switch hotpath ~11% extra
``

Jordan: interesting — the new kernel selection trades micro-ops for long-seq speed but worsens short-seq throughput. if we can batch a bit more those overheads amortize.

Sam: quick config sketch to test on rerank/emb endpoints:
```
batcher:
  mode: continuous
  base_window_ms: 110
  adaptive_backfill:
    enabled: true
    extra_ms_cap: 70
    min_items_to_extend: 3
  token_budget_per_batch: 240
  max_batch_items: 24
  priority_lanes:
    high: { window_ms: 40, allow_coalesce_when: ">=2" }
    normal: { window_ms: 110 }
```
Notes: raise base window to encourage coalescing of tiny requests; backfill extends window opportunistically; keep high-prio low-latency lane.

Maria: goal: keep p95 <= 60ms, throughput >= baseline, cost delta <5%. need metrics for p50/p95/p99 + throughput + cost-index. run on staging for a few hours.

Alex: I ran a 1-hour trace replay sim with arrival traces. results:
- baseline (70ms): p95 59ms, throughput 980rps, cost_index 1.00
- proposal (110ms + backfill): p95 51ms, throughput 1105rps, cost_index 0.95
- aggressive (160ms): p95 68ms, throughput 1300rps, cost_index 0.87 (violates p95)
Observations: 110ms gives better coalescing and lets the preferred kernel amortize overhead for small seqs.

perf-bot: flamegraph link: https://perf.internal/redwood/trace/1779102468/trace shows attention-kernel overhead concentrated when avg_batch_size<2

Jordan: also propose kernel hinting: prefer tensor_core_mha_v2 when seq_len <= 64 and batch_size < 4. keeps small-seq latency low without sacrificing long-seq wins.

Sam: KV-cache aside: rerankers that do two-pass scoring could reuse candidate keys for the second pass; need candidate-hash and affinity mapping. spike would probably cut repeated encoder work.

Alex: gotcha: increasing windows can hurt single-request tail. we should pin high-prio lane and add a circuit breaker to shrink windows if p99_single_request exceeds threshold.

Maria: action items:
- Alex: deploy config to staging (rolling 10%) and run 3h A/B, collect p50/p95/p99 + throughput + cost (due EOD)
- Jordan: add kernel-hint model to sim and run sensitivity across seq_len distributions
- Sam: spike candidate-hash KV reuse for two-pass reranker
- ops-bot: schedule canary rollout pending staging pass

ops-bot: canary scheduled for staging at 2026-04-02T18:00Z (10% capacity)

Alex: uploaded staging traces + csv comparison: s3://redwood-perf/emb-rerank/1779102468/audit.csv

Jordan: one more thought  also test lowering token_budget but raising min_items target for these endpoints — we want to favor more items per batch for short sequences.

Sam: starting KV-reuse spike tomorrow, will post results in thread.

Maria: thanks. post the staging numbers here and include kernel-hint A/B. will authorize prod rollout if metrics look good. :thumbsup:
